title: Claims Integrity Audit: Modifier 25 Unbundling Review (CPT 99214-25 with Arthrocentesis 20610)
requested_service: CPT 99214-25 (E/M Office Visit Moderate MDM with Modifier 25) + CPT 20610 (Arthrocentesis Major Joint)
unstructured_note:
ORTHOPEDIC CLINIC PROCEDURE NOTE
Date of Service: October 12, 2026
Patient: Gerald Foster (DOB: 03/19/1959, Age: 67, Male)
Attending Surgeon: Dr. Gregory Vance, MD

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Scheduled visit for planned right knee corticosteroid injection for persistent osteoarthritis pain.

HISTORY & EXAMINATION:
Patient reports ongoing right medial knee pain previously diagnosed as grade 3 primary osteoarthritis. Pain is exacerbated by prolonged standing. Denies recent falls or acute trauma. Denies fever or chills.
Focused Exam: Right knee demonstrates mild suprapatellar fullness, medial joint line tenderness. Range of motion 0 to 125 degrees without mechanical block. Neurovascular exam intact distally.

PROCEDURAL TIMEOUT & INFORMED CONSENT:
Informed consent obtained after discussing risks including infection, bleeding, transient hyperglycemia, post-injection flare, and tendon injury. Patient elected to proceed.

PROCEDURE DETAILS (CPT 20610):
The right knee was prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion using ChloraPrep. Under sterile technique, a 21-gauge 1.5-inch needle was inserted via anterolateral approach into the right synovial space. 2 mL of clear yellowish synovial fluid was aspirated. Subsequently, a mixture of 40 mg triamcinolone acetonide (Kenalog) and 3 mL of 1% plain lidocaine was injected without resistance. Needle withdrawn, sterile bandage applied. Patient tolerated procedure well without immediate adverse events. Discharged with post-injection activity guidance.

BILLING & CODING SUBMISSION:
- CPT 20610: Arthrocentesis, aspiration and/or injection, major joint (right knee)
- CPT 99214-25: Office or other outpatient visit for the evaluation and management of an established patient, moderate medical decision making, with Modifier 25 indicating a significant, separately identifiable evaluation.
